per_problem.decision: Retain confirmed Minor for the stated unrestricted radial-derivative closure.
per_problem.reasoning: I checked Definition 1.2's strict k>0, the absence of central input in Proposition 3.1(2), and the proof's explicit later use of centrality. For ell(A)=tr(diag(1,2)A), g=ell^2 has g(I)=9, real roots from (3t+ell(A))^2, and cone ell>0 containing all positive definite A. The radial derivative q=6ell has gradient diag(6,12), not central. At diag(3/2,2/3), det A=1 and q(A)=17<18=q(I), so the erroneous closure could not justify applying the determinant bound to q. Separately, g=tr A is central of degree one but its radial derivative is the constant 2 with zero gradient. For central input of degree N>=2, differentiated Euler homogeneity gives Dq(I)=(N-1)Dg(I), and Rolle interlacing preserves the Garding-Dirichlet cone property. The source proof stops at degree one and the main theorem does not use this supplementary closure statement.

per_problem.decision: Retain confirmed Minor for the reverse hyperbolicity implication for arbitrary L.
per_problem.reasoning: With g=det on Sym(3), J=diag(1,-1,-1) and L(A)=tr(A)J/3, the original g is itself central Garding-Dirichlet and g_L=(tr(A)/3)^3 is nonzero of degree three. It is I-hyperbolic with g_L(I)=1. Direct expansion of the 2x2 block in tJ+E12+E21 gives det=t(t^2+1), disproving ambient J-hyperbolicity while meeting the printed assumptions. The later cone-preserving and scaled-identity conditions are separate clauses, not hypotheses of (a). The printed factorization tests only Im L. The forward implication is valid; surjectivity restores the converse by lifting every ambient test matrix. The main Lemma 2.4 uses invertible congruence and hh^t>0, so this error is not a counterexample to its use or to Theorem 1.3.

per_problem.decision: Retain confirmed_under_explicit_arbitrary_L_scope, Minor; do not promote to an unconditional defect under the nonzero-pullback interpretation.
per_problem.reasoning: The actual PDF has the closure bar in L(P) subset bar Gamma. For g=det on Sym(2), L(A)=a11 E11 maps every positive semidefinite input into bar Gamma but g_L is identically zero, violating g_L(I)>0. The proof on p.12 instead assumes L(P)>0. However, if the introductory degree-N wording is treated as an independent nonzero-pullback hypothesis, this example is inadmissible and the conclusion is valid. Indeed a nonzero polynomial g_L cannot vanish on the open positive cone, so some P0>0 has L(P0) in Gamma; choosing cI-P0>=0 then gives cL(I)=L(P0)+L(cI-P0) in Gamma+bar Gamma subset Gamma. Conversely L(I) in Gamma implies g_L nonzero. With that condition, P=epsilon I+(P-epsilon I) proves L(P) in Gamma for every P>0, and valid forward pullback hyperbolicity proves the claim. Part (f)'s L(I)=kI, k>0 also supplies nondegeneracy when combined with (e); its chain-rule/trace argument is valid. The existing report already states these restrictions and needs no correction.

per_problem.decision: Retain confirmed Minor for the named I-eigenvalue and Laplacian normalization.
per_problem.reasoning: The source fixes g(tI+A)=g(I) product(t+lambda_j^I(A)). Homogeneity at A=I forces every normalized I-eigenvalue to equal 1. The displayed Lagrangian factors at I_(2n) equal n because the skew-Hermitian component vanishes; they therefore cannot be normalized I-eigenvalues when n>1. For n=2, N=4, the actual polynomial is 16(t+1)^4; using the displayed factors as normalized roots gives 16(t+2)^4 and values 16 versus 256 at t=0. Since each factor shifts by nt under A -> A+tI, the correct roots are Lambda/n and their sum is 2^(n-1) tr(A)/n. The unnormalized sign-sum itself is valid, the corrected sum remains a positive scalar multiple of trace, and the sharp determinant prefactor g(I)^(1/N)=n remains unchanged. There is no discrepancy for n=1.

per_problem.decision: Retain the rejection of the proposed completeness objection.
per_problem.reasoning: I actually inspected the saved earlier primary reference pp.7,20,21: completeness is expressed as P intersect E={0} for the edge, while zero edge in the whole matrix space is a separate regularity condition. A nonzero positive semidefinite P in the edge would have Dg(I)[P]=0, contrary to centrality k tr(P)>0. Thus the trace-power example does not refute the authors' completeness statement under their documented meaning.

per_problem.decision: Support the report's Minor overall assessment and stated limits.
per_problem.reasoning: I independently reconstructed Basic Lemma 2.1 from nonnegative coefficients: w_alpha=a_alpha/p(e) sum to 1 and Euler/centrality give sum w_alpha alpha_j=N/n. Weighted logarithmic concavity yields p(x)>=p(e)(product x_j)^(N/n); equality depends on coefficient support and need not force scalar matrices. The universal orthogonal-basis condition and conjugation of the gradient then establish Theorem 2.3. Garding directional differentiation at fixed epsilon in directions e_j+epsilon e, followed by the limit of the entire N-linear derivative expression, supplies nonnegative diagonal coefficients for Theorem 1.3 without assuming an epsilon-independent intermediate vector. The degree-one endpoint and possible zero coefficients cause no failure. For Proposition 1.6, f=g^(1/N), concavity and Euler give f(A)<=tr(Df(B)A); the determinant-one trace infimum forces Df(B)>0 and is n(det Df(B))^(1/n). The converse follows from Euler and matrix AM-GM. Hence Corollary 1.7's constant g(I)^(n/N)/n^n is correct. Product closure has positive central gradient by the product rule. None of the four local findings is required for this verified main proof. Foundational Garding cone/concavity results and the original Lagrangian construction remain imported, not fully re-proved.
